I farm by keeping things steady and manageable. I am 67, my household is small, and I have 16.1 mu with well irrigation, so I will not spread myself too thin or chase risky changes. Because my main system is wheat-maize, I will keep most of the land in that rotation and leave a smaller part for stevia, which gives me some cash income but needs more careful field management. I will use seeds that I trust and inputs at a moderate level: enough fertilizer to protect yield, enough irrigation to avoid drought stress, and only a limited number of pesticide sprays when pressure shows up. For wheat, I will stay with improved seed, keep the field fairly clean, irrigate at key stages, and aim for a stable grain yield. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because maize responds well and gives me stronger yield on the same land after wheat. For stevia, I will keep the area smaller because it takes more attention, but I will still feed and water it well so the return is worthwhile. I will mostly use rotary tillage because it saves labor and fits the way I manage land now.
